summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of HfO2, Al2O3, and HfAlOx using TDEAH and TDEAA as metal precursors with ozone as the oxidizer. The ALD process was characterized by self-limiting kinetics, with ALD rates of 1.1 Å/cycle for HfO2 and 1.3 Å/cycle for Al2O3. The overlapping temperature windows of 200–275 °C allowed for the deposition of composite HfAlOx films. The films were analyzed using FTIR, XPS, and XRD, revealing interfacial oxide growth, hydroxyl and nitrate groups, and crystallization behavior upon annealing.
evidence: Tetrakis-diethylamino hafnium (TDEAH), tris-diethylamino aluminum (TDEAA), and ozone were used for the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of HfO2, Al2O3, and HfAlOx films. The ALD rates were measured to be 1.1 Å/cycle for HfO2 and 1.3 Å/cycle for Al2O3. The ALD temperature windows were found to be between 200 and 325 °C for TDEAA, and between 200 and 275 °C for TDEAH. The overlap of these ALD windows between 200 and 275 °C is critical for ALD of the composite film, HfAlOx.
